e-bikes tolerate slope substantially better than conventional bicycles (the pilot's frozen methodology treats slope as comfortable below 3.0 deg, still e-bike-manageable up to 10.0 deg, with a floor of 0.5 to avoid rewarding perfectly flat terrain arbitrarily), but very steep terrain remains operationally undesirable regardless of motor assistance (safety, battery drain, braking). Treated as COST with a shallow-then-steepening penalty, not a simple linear cost, reusing the frozen pilot thresholds rather than inventing new ones.
Share of cell area in the mildly-sloped band -- supports a piecewise/threshold value function alongside mean_slope_deg.
Share of cell area approaching the steep threshold -- distinguishes cells with a mild mean slope but a substantial steep sub-area from uniformly mild cells.
Complementary share; retaining the two higher bands is sufficient to characterize the slope profile without triple-counting (all four bands sum to 100%).
Correlated with mean_slope_deg/max_slope_deg at this resolution; the two retained mid-range bands already capture the comfortable-to-steep transition relevant to e-bikes.
